about: REAL Indian health records behind anumaan/realcheck_india.py: HMIS district-month totals (the Total column) for the items and stock ledgers that the pre-registered rules in realcheck_india_rules.json use. series holds every district-year whose IFA (19.6), IFA syrup (19.9) or albendazole (19.15) ledger is in use. An item is 12 monthly values, April to March; a ledger is its 5 fields (in the order of the rules' ledger_fields) x 12 months; prev_close is the previous March's Total Stock, null where that year was not fetched or the cell was blank; null is a blank cell. summary() recomputes results from series. files, fetched, coverage, series and results are rewritten by: python -m anumaan.realcheck_india --fetch DIR

source.dataset: HMIS Standard Reports, C2 'Data Itemwise Monthly (up to sub district)': 'All States and Districts Across Months'
source.publisher: Health Management Information System (HMIS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India
source.licence: The HMIS portal states no open licence. Its Terms of Use say the content is provided by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare 'for the information to general public' and that it is 'for reference purposes only'. The same item-wise monthly HMIS reports are published on the Open Government Data Platform (data.gov.in) under the Government Open Data License - India (GODL-India).
source.attribution: Source: HMIS, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.
source.note: One zip per financial year, one table per state or UT inside, district x month x item, with five sub-columns per month (Total, Public, Private, Urban, Rural); only Total is used. Every file is headed 'Provisional Figures' with a 'Status As On' date (see coverage). Only the official zips are used, never a third party's parsed copy.

caveats: Premise only, at district-month grain, on self-reported aggregates. It asks whether stock-outs that a district's own HMIS store ledger records coincide with fewer full courses of that medicine in the same district's HMIS care counts. Anumaan's filter never runs here: nothing is per PHC or per day, and no HMIS record links a diagnosis to a prescription.

Not hidden stock-outs. The marker is the register itself, while Anumaan's claim is that care reveals what the register hides, so this can show at most that stock-outs the register records leave the fingerprint. EMPTY means no reporting store in the district had any IFA to issue, which is rare: 132 scored EMPTY months in FY 2017-20.

Only districts whose ledger is in use count: all five fields reported every month, and something distributed in 6 or more. For IFA that is 81, 84 and 110 of 704 districts in FY 2017-18, 2018-19 and 2019-20. They are not a sample of India.
Not independent records. The ledger and the care counts come from the same monthly HMIS form, filled in by the same staff. The gap guard and the calcium placebo cover this only partly.

Small numbers. 8 of the 132 EMPTY months were flagged, so one or two flags move the ratio a lot, and the 95% CI runs from 0.27 to 3.80. Inconclusive means neither the support rule nor the refutation rule was met; it is not weak support.

By the pre-registered reading the calcium placebo is quiet (its CI reaches 0), but its rate ratio equals the primary's: 1.65 (95% CI 0.00 to 3.95), 5 of 53 months flagged when the IFA ledger was empty and calcium stocked, against 73 of 1,274 with both stocked. So the small excess of flags in EMPTY months is not shown to be specific to IFA.

FY 2019-20 alone (v0) meets the refutation rule: 1 of 70 EMPTY months flagged against 33 of 973 STOCKED months, rate ratio 0.42 (95% CI 0.00 to 1.50). The rules made the three years (v1) the headline before any result was seen.

A null here would not settle the question for PHC dispensing: IFA handed out from stores outside the district ledger (sub-centres, ASHAs) would dilute the fingerprint. Anemia Mukt Bharat scaled IFA up from 2018, and the baselines, a district-year's own STOCKED months, have no trend term.

Every file is headed 'Provisional Figures', with status as on 15 Mar 2019 (FY 2017-18), 10 Jan 2020 (2018-19) and 06 Nov 2020 (2019-20). The same 704 district names appear in all three years, and every item name matches the rules.

Known exposure before the rules were written. Another agent on this project had run a crude feasibility probe on a third party's parsed copy of the same HMIS files. For adult IFA it compared the ledger's own 'Stock Distributed' per ANC registration in and after months whose closing stock hit zero, and it reported the month after a zero close as informative. It never used items 1.2.4, 1.2.5, 9.9 or 9.10. The rules transcribe a design written after that probe, and their EMPTY month (nothing opening or received, after a month that closed at zero) is close to that month; whether the design's author saw the probe is not recorded. The rules' own author had seen only the probe's first lines when writing them.
Reproducible: python -m anumaan.realcheck_india --fetch DIR rebuilds this file from the official zips, whose sha256 are listed under files, and summary() recomputes every figure from series.

amendments.what: Telangana's FY 2017-18 file is read from an .xlsx workbook, with the standard library.
amendments.why: The rules describe every file as a SAS-HTML table saved as .xls, and 116 of the 117 files are. Telangana 2017-18 is a real .xlsx with the same columns (district, code, name, type, then five sub-columns for each of 12 months and a total), but it stores codes that look like numbers as numbers (9.10 reads 9.1, 19.6 reads 19.600000000000001). There, codes are matched as numbers; the item names printed in every year are recorded in coverage and match the rules' names. Decided before any outcome was computed.

amendments.what: In the two raw-count replications (9.9 against ledger 19.9, 9.10 against ledger 19.15), a month whose reference has median 0 and MAD 0 has a zero scale, because the MAD floor is 1% of a zero median, so its z is undefined. Such a month stays scored and is not flagged: its count is 0 or more, never below the reference median, so it shows no dip.
amendments.why: The rules do not define z when the scale is zero. Only the secondaries are affected: the primary and both placebos floor the MAD at 0.01 absolute. This was found after the first results were computed, when an independent re-implementation cross-checked them; both implementations already handled it this way before any result was seen. Leaving those months out instead changes no label: FY 2019-20 albendazole goes from 1 of 69 EMPTY months flagged against 9 of 880 STOCKED (rate ratio 1.42) to 1 of 61 against 9 of 692 (1.26); FY 2017-20 IFA syrup goes from 2.02 to 2.06 and albendazole from 0.79 to 0.76; FY 2019-20 IFA syrup has no such month. Zero-scale months: 213 for albendazole in FY 2019-20; 49 for IFA syrup and 468 for albendazole in FY 2017-20. None has a negative count.
